svg.title: One interval survives all exceptional twists
svg.desc: Computed with the induction of UpperTheory.V.Win.window1 on the book's example: forbidden logarithmic intervals [a, B a) for a = 8, 90 with B = 2 inside [0, 128]; the recursion lowers the ceiling 128 -> 32 and returns [16, 32], i.e. [Y, Y^2] = [2^16, 2^32].

text.font-family: Inter, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif

svg.text: u = log₂ x (forbidden: [a, 2a) for each exceptional twist h, a = log₂(h)/C_t)

svg.text: ceiling U = 128: start 90 lies in (32, 128] → delete it

svg.text: ceiling U′ = 128/(2B) = 32: no start in (8, 32] → y = U′/2 = 16

svg.text: Ultrametric separation (ℓ = 3, Z = 80, centre 1): |h − 1|₃ < 3⁻³ forces h ≡ 1 mod 81, so h = 1 only;

text.font-family: Inter, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif

svg.text: with ≤ instead of < one would also admit 28 and 55. Each ℓ-adic centre produces at most one exceptional twist.
